hypothesis: The sampling needed to resolve curvature follows from two terms of a local quadratic fit: a bias set by the quartic profile term and a noise term that grows as the window shrinks; the window must be chosen from the actual profile, not from its osculating circle.
input_data: Declared scanner noise 0.01 mm per point, native spacing 0.05 mm
Profiles: coupon crest (Gaussian), cylinder circumference (R = 100 mm), flat plate
Seeded synthetic noise (PCG64 seed 20260926), 4000 fits per window, 2000 registrations
mathematical_model: Least-squares z = a + b x + c x^2 over a centred window W with spacing d: bias(2c) = (3/7) q W^2, std(2c) = sigma sqrt(720 d) W^(-5/2) (large-n); tolerance split half bias, half k = 2 noise. Registration: Kabsch; E[SSR] = sigma^2 (3N - 6); rotation covariance sigma^2 (sum |p|^2 I - p p^T)^-1.
numerical_result: Coupon crest at 5%: window 13.66 mm, spacing 0.646 mm; repeats at 0.05 mm native spacing: 5% -> 1, 2% -> 5, 1% -> 109; circle rule gives bias 1.96 x tolerance.
observation_model: Synthetic scans only; no scanner was used.

physical_validation_status.statement: Physical validation requires acquired hardware evidence; none was acquired for this task.

title: Define a surface metrology protocol.
uncertainty: Monte Carlo standard errors are stated in the checks; the design rules are exact for the declared profiles.
unresolved_assumptions: Surface finish, incidence angle and scanner nonlinearity are not modelled; noise is white and Gaussian.
Profiles are taken through the principal direction at the vertex; slope correction is neglected.
At 1% tolerance a quadratic fit needs about 100 repeat scans: a higher-order local fit is a deferred research question.
